passage: Friday night. Today I noticed a supplier invoice had been entered twice. A small thing. But in our team, after what happened to Keerthana last month, shouted at in front of everyone over a wrong figure, nobody says anything out loud. I sat with it for two hours. Then I quietly deleted one entry and told nobody. If I reported it, I would be the next name on the whiteboard. Now the total is right, but whatever caused it is still there, and two others probably enter invoices the same way. I feel like I'm covering tracks, and I hate that. It should not feel dangerous to say "I got this wrong." - Dilnaz

qa.q: What did Dilnaz notice on Friday?
qa.a: Dilnaz noticed that a supplier invoice had been entered twice.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling about quietly deleting the entry and telling nobody?
qa.a: Uneasy and ashamed, feeling like covering tracks and afraid of being blamed.

qa.q: What could the team do to make reporting mistakes safer?
qa.a: Respond to reported errors by asking what happened instead of shouting, so people can speak up.

qa.q: How did Keerthana's experience last month affect the team?
qa.a: Being shouted at in front of everyone taught the others to stay silent about problems.

grounding: Shows a worker in a punishing team hiding a small problem so it can grow unseen.

passage:
Lalit: the wrong label batch went out on Tuesday. only I know
Mahima: you didn't tell the manager?
Lalit: after last month's meeting when someone got named in front of everyone? no way
Mahima: I know. but if the customer finds it first it's worse 😟
Lalit: I've already reprinted the labels and swapped the boxes in the store. quietly
Mahima: so nobody knows the printer settings caused it?
Lalit: right. and it will happen again 😔
Mahima: what if we raise it Monday as a process problem, not your mistake?
Lalit: I'd have to trust it won't be used against me
Mahima: I'll speak first and say I nearly did the same. deal?
Lalit: ...ok. deal 🙂

qa.q: On which day did the wrong label batch go out?
qa.a: The wrong label batch went out on Tuesday.

qa.q: Why did Lalit keep the mistake quiet?
qa.a: Lalit was afraid of being named and blamed in front of everyone, as happened in last month's meeting.
Raising it on Monday as a process problem, with Mahima speaking first and saying that Mahima nearly did the same.
That a customer will find the mistake first, and that the problem will return because the printer settings remain unfixed.

grounding: Shows a worker in a blame culture hiding a problem while a colleague tries to move it into the open.
